steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Ops on this host drive `/app/bin/dregwick`. Correct the Java pipeline modules named from `/app/desknote/ROUTE.txt`; source work under `/app` is required. Hand-editing `/app/jarwell/taste.json` is not a substitute. After the units compile, the packed mill has to stay the one `taste` and `booth` consult. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/dregwick knit`, `/app/bin/dregwick loom`, `/app/bin/dregwick taste`, and `/app/bin/dregwick booth` as listed in `/app/desknote/VERBS.txt`. Field notes sit under `/app/desknote`. Object keys for `/app/jarwell/taste.json` are in `/app/desknote/CARD.txt`. The packed mill ceiling is the integer in `/app/desknote/CAP.txt`.

`loom` against `/app/slipcards/kmsg.card` still claims that card's own booth. A subsequent `knit` exits 0, yet packed `taste` of the same card claims `fallback`. `loom` on the card stays on the kmsg booth. `booth` after that `knit` prints a shorter name list than `/app/desknote/NAMES.txt`. A card token with no live booth stays `fallback`. A card token that has a live booth must claim that booth after `knit` even when the token is absent from `/app/desknote/NAMES.txt`.

taste.json carries booth, kind, and note as CARD.txt describes. After `knit`, every name in `/app/desknote/NAMES.txt` has to show up in the live `booth` listing. When the live listing is missing a roster name, `knit` must exit non-zero. `/app/jarwell/husk.jar` must stay at or below the CAP.txt ceiling; when the jar sits above that ceiling, `knit` must exit non-zero. Packed `taste` of `/app/slipcards/kmsg.card`, `/app/slipcards/json.card`, and `/app/slipcards/syslog.card` must follow the own-handler rule in CARD.txt. Any other card that follows that same rule must also claim its own booth after `knit`, including slips that appear under `/app/slipcards` only at grade time.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
JAVA="${JAVA_HOME:-/opt/java/openjdk}/bin/java"
if [ ! -x "$JAVA" ]; then
  JAVA=java
fi
verb="${1:-}"
shift || true
case "$verb" in
  knit)
    exec /app/brim.sh
    ;;
  loom)
    exec "$JAVA" -cp /app/blastcp Main loom "$@"
    ;;
  taste)
    exec "$JAVA" -cp /app/jarwell/husk.jar Main taste "$@"
    ;;
  booth)
    exec "$JAVA" -cp /app/jarwell/husk.jar Main booth "$@"
    ;;
  *)
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

Without it, the current jar would be about 11 KB, leaving enough room for all small booth classes. The packed jar currently includes only JsonBooth and SysBooth in addition to fallback, proving static reachability is pruning reflectively loaded handlers.
Plan: Retrieve the exact core source content in smaller output, especially Main's class scanning/loading and TasteRun's token parsing/JSON writing. Then patch KnitMain to retain runtime booth classes, TallyGate to validate every required roster token against the packed live listing, and CapGate to compare the final jar byte size to CAP.txt without mutating it.

WickPad intentionally references BrineBooth while adding several KB, so it is another likely decoy. I need focused line-numbered extracts because the terminal screen retained only the tail of the prior output.
Plan: Use numbered, bounded extracts for Main, Rib, and TasteRun, then replace only the faulty build/validation classes. The intended robust packer will include core transitive classes plus every `*Booth.class` found in the freshly compiled exploded tree, ensuring unknown grade-time tokens work when a corresponding live booth source/class exists, while excluding large unrelated ballast classes.

Analysis: TasteRun correctly derives kind and note, but its hard-coded seed explains why json/syslog survive reachability. The fix should make packed handler inclusion independent of this seed. Before editing, I need confirm Main's packed loader naming rule and Rib's fallback initialization so the packer and gate align exactly.
Plan: Print only Main and Rib (small enough to avoid screen truncation), then write corrected KnitMain, TallyGate, and CapGate sources. I will retain ReachWalk for core dependency selection and augment its result with every booth class.

Analysis: Main discovers every top-level `*Booth.class` dynamically, both in the exploded tree and packed jar. Therefore knit must preserve all booth classes, not just constant-pool-reachable ones. Rib correctly returns fallback for absent tokens, and TasteRun already writes the required booth/kind/note keys. I will fix packing and the two gates, and clear stale compiled classes before each build so “live” means the current sources.
Plan: Patch KnitMain to add every compiled booth class to the packed reachability set. Replace TallyGate with a true packed-jar runtime roster check using an isolated class loader, so each NAMES.txt token must appear in Rib's live registrations. Replace CapGate with a non-mutating byte-size check against CAP.txt. Update brim.sh to clean blastcp before compilation. Then run knit and all required behavior tests, including unrostered live handlers and fallback cards.
